## Wave NPC1e — the arc's close (2026-08-28)

Base `077698d9`. The certification wave, and the last of the five. Four waves
built a crowd — a tier ladder, a renderer that reads it, a route substrate and a
society that walks one — and each handed this one a list. What NPC1e owes is
three things: the routed cost items taken in **measured order**, the ten walls
the arc was briefed against given their **final disposition**, and the island
measured at the hour its town is on the street, with whatever remains attributed
by name.

**The headline, first and unflattering: 60 fps p50 is not met at any N, and it
was not met at N = 0.** The island alone has never reached it — wave I8c
certified `LIT+VIS` at 24.270 ms p50 and wrote *"≥ 60 fps p50 LIT+VIS is STILL
NOT MET"* as the carried headline, on a serial harness whose CPU half alone was
13.879 ms; this wave reads `LIT+VIS` at **25.319 ms, 39.5 fps**, and the row with
a **hand-installed empty population** — the only true N = 0 in the list — at
**24.554 ms, 40.7 fps**.
*(The NPC1e audit's note: the plain `LIT+VIS` row is taken **before** the first
`set_crowd_population(Default)` in the row order, so the society the level derives
for itself is still deriving under it — at the authored player start that census
is **1 000 agents, 998 of them `Far`**, which is the staging finding below. So
25.319 is the island **with its own resident crowd at the cheapest tier**, and
the N = 0 number to quote against I8c's 24.270 is the crowd-control row's
24.554. Both miss 60 fps and the headline stands; the row it was hung on did
not.)* What is new is the
crowd's share, and it is large: a player standing in the thickest part of the
island's own rush hour, among a thousand residents the level derived for itself,
reads **241.748 ms p50 — 4.1 fps** — of which **84 ms is one station**. So this
wave lands on **clause D** of the brief rather than clause A, and it lands there
with a mechanism on every line rather than with a shrug.

**And it lands with a law it did not expect to find.** The arc has spent three
waves quoting *"0.18 ms a character in the mover"* as a constant, and the NPC1c
audit certified it as *"genuinely linear"* over a 64× range in N. It is not a
constant. It is **0.494 ms a character** when a hundred and ninety-one people are
inside a thirty-two metre ring, and the reason no arm saw it is that no arm swept
**density** — a fact this wave measured on a fixture a tenth the island's size
before it wrote it down.

### The levers, in measured order

The brief routed five cost items with their mechanisms. Four are taken and
measured; the fifth is refused for the second time, at the current numbers.

### Lever 1 — the mover, and the table the arc aimed with

The NPC1c audit's special investigation ended with a verdict and a direction:
*"the wave's 0.18 ms a character is genuinely linear per-character movement work
against a 17 823-body city… the lever is fewer or cheaper queries per character
— a coarser probe set, a cached ground answer, or a mover that is not
collide-and-slide — and the **ground** is where to aim it first."* It named the
station and stopped one level above the query.

**So the queries were priced one at a time**, on the island's own tile
resolution, in `character_move_cost::where_the_movers_queries_go` — and after
the NPC1e audit's correction below, **every row is a cast that HIT**:

| the primitive, in the mover's own fixture world (1 854 bodies) | µs |
|---|---|
| `move_character` — rapier's sweep, its ground snap and its autostep | **25.8** |
| the same with **autostep off** | 25.5 (≈1 %, inside the spread) |
| the same with the **ground snap off** | 25.8 (same) |
| the section-9 **ground-normal probe**, one `cast_shape` into the height field | **5.62** |
| the same probe dropped onto a **building's roof** — a `Collider3D` box | **0.50** |
| the same depth as a downward **ray** into the height field | **0.25** |

Two things fall out. The first is that *"four heightfield tiles cost more than
1 849 buildings"* is right at the primitive, and the honest size of it is
**11.3×** — one cast that hits a height-field tile against one that hits a box,
in the same world, the same tree and the same filter — with the isolated
one-body control in `what_a_cast_against_the_ground_costs` reading **2.9×**
(1.034 µs a tile against 0.356 a slab). The second is that neither knob the mover
exposes matters — autostep and the ground snap are each about one per cent — so
the lever is the *number and the shape* of the casts, not their configuration.
**And the shape is the bigger lever of the two**: a ray that reaches the same
depth answers the same ground **22×** cheaper than the swept sphere in the
fixture, and **45×** cheaper on the ground-only world.

> **CORRECTION (the NPC1e audit, 2026-08-28).** The first cut of this section
> published the probe at **0.07 µs "against 1 849 building boxes"** and read
> **75×** out of it — a number that then became one of the wave's closing laws
> and one of its carried prescriptions. That row is the fixture's
> `ground(false)` world, where the character has been in **free fall since the
> settle loop** — the very body this wave corrected the four-world table for —
> so it stands a hundred metres beneath every box and its probe **hits nothing
> at all**. 0.07 µs is a broad phase saying "no", and 5.6 ÷ 0.07 is a hit
> divided by a miss. The published **ray at 0.18 µs** was a miss for a second
> reason and had **no arm behind it at all**: a ray of `probe_len` stops *above*
> the ground the sphere's radius reaches, and nothing in
> `character_move_cost.rs` measured a ray until this audit added one. Both are
> now measured against hits, and the arm asserts `probe_hit == spec.ground` and
> `ray_hit == probe_hit`, so the table cannot be quoted across that gap again.
> **The law this wave paid for, it paid twice and banked once.**

**AND THE TABLE THE ARC AIMED WITH IS CORRECTED.** The NPC1c audit's four-world
decomposition used `travelled_m > 1.0` as its anti-vacuity clause, and a body in
**free fall travels further than one that walks**. Both ground-free rows end at
**y = −139.056 m** having never touched anything, at **3.00 queries a step**
against a walking body's **1.00** — an airborne step runs `predict_landing` and
takes no ground probe, so the two halves are *different programs* and their
"additive to within 4 %" is a coincidence across that gap. `Measured` carries
`grounded`, `end_y` and queries-per-character-step now, prints them in the table,
and asserts the shape both ways so nobody reads it that way again.

**The lever, and it is exact rather than approximate.**
`MovementRuntime::ground_normal` has **exactly one reader in the engine** — grep
it — `slide_friction`, inside section 7's `MovementMode::Slide` branch. So
`movement::reads_the_ground_normal` takes the probe for a character that is
sliding or holding sprint (the one door into `Slide`) and for nobody else. A
walking crowd agent has no input at all and never asks. The one-step bound the
predicate carries is stated on the function rather than implied.

**Measured, on one machine, with the probe forced on and then shipped:**

| | probe on | NPC1e |
|---|---|---|
| N = 1 | 52.18 µs a character | **47.82** (−8.3 %) |
| N = 64 | 52.46 | **48.49** (−7.6 %) |
| queries a character a step | 2.00 | **1.00** |

…and **on the island**: the isolated fixed step's `character move` reads
**0.129 → 0.101 ms**, and the arc's own N = 1 000 row reads **3.661** and
**4.921** across this wave's two full runs of the instrument against **5.630**
and **5.585** in the two waves before. Better in both, and the *spread* is
published rather than the best of them — this is the station the certification
row shows is a function of crowd **density**, so a number from it is a number
about where that flight's crowd happened to stand.

**It is armed as a COUNT, not a clock** — the NPC1c CI-red's own law, four
payments in. `PhysicsWorld3D::queries` is bumped in `ensure_query_pipeline`, the
one door every ray, shape cast, intersection and mover call goes through, so
"the mover asks the world twice and now asks once" is a subtraction.
`a_walking_character_asks_the_world_once_and_a_sprinting_one_twice` asserts 1 and
2 exactly and then reads the sprinter's normal back, so an arm that only counted
could not pass on a probe whose answer was thrown away.

### Lever 2 — the fifth skinned consumer stops walking a crowd per joint

The NPC1b audit's finding 6, routed here with its number: `passes::gi` is the
**fifth** consumer of `RenderScene::skinned` and the only one that walks it **per
joint**. At N = 1 000 that is `1 001 × 161 ≈ 161 000` oriented boxes staged a
frame — each an `inverse()` and a 112-byte push — nearly all of them thrown away
by the volume clip, and the `gi` pass's CPU recording went **0.162 → 0.778 ms**
for a pass a crowd adds one draw to. The routing said what was missing: *"a
conservative per-instance pre-reject the staging path has no bound for today."*

`gi::skinned_model_bound` is that bound. It unions the per-joint bind boxes the
pass already caches, carried through the instance's own palette, as an AABB and
then circumscribes it; `gi::skinned_world_bound` lifts the result through the
model matrix with its **Frobenius norm**, which upper-bounds the operator norm
and therefore survives a non-uniform or sheared instance scale. The staging
loop's own bound is `centre = (model · Jⱼ) · cⱼ`, `radius = Σᵢ hᵢ |(model · Jⱼ)ᵢ|`,
so the algebra is one line and it is written on the function.

**Memoized on `(mesh, palette pointer)` in a map local to the call.** A crowd's
far tier shares one rest-pose palette `Arc` between every agent of an archetype,
so the bound is derived once for hundreds of instances — and because the map
lives for the call while the scene is borrowed for it, no key can outlive its
allocation. That is `plan_skinned_batches`' argument and deliberately not the
field-cache shape, which would have to hold the `Arc`.

**It fails open**: a non-finite palette answers `None`, which the caller reads as
*"stage it"*; an all-degenerate mesh answers a zero radius, which is what the
staging loop would have emitted anyway.

**Measured on the island**, against the same adjacent bracket:
`gi` CPU recording **0.165 → 0.310 ms (+0.144)** where NPC1b's was
**0.162 → 0.778 (+0.62)** — the crowd's share of that pass is **4.3× smaller**.
`GiAudit::skinned_rejected` reads **1 001 a frame**: the whole crowd, dropped
before a joint is touched.

### Lever 3 — the leg is resolved once a step, not five times an agent

NPC1d carried it as item 11: the island's 329 **scheduled** residents read
`crowd` **0.353 ms — 1.07 µs an agent —** against the instrument's thousand
ping-pong walkers at **0.164 ms, 0.16 µs**. **6.5×**, with one lever named and
refused: caching the leg index *on the record* is a second copy of a pure
function, and this module has refused two of those already.

**This is the other lever**, and it is the P29.4-A8 shape rather than a cache:
resolve it once and hand it down. `step_crowd_banded` asked
`CrowdRecord::leg_at` **four times an agent** — the leg-change check, then
`progress_at`, then `position_at → feet_at → {path_at, progress_at}` again — and
a *steered* agent a fifth time inside the pursuit. Each is a `mix64` and a
`rem_euclid` plus a `rem_euclid` a leg, for an answer that cannot change inside a
step. `crowd::ActiveLeg` is the resolved answer; every `*_at` door keeps its
signature and delegates to a new `*_on` sibling that takes it. Nothing is stored,
so nothing can drift — which is the distinction the refused lever could not make.

`SteerSubject` **loses** its `guid` and its `clock`, and that is the point rather
than tidying: they existed only so the pursuit could re-derive the leg.

**Armed as an equality, to the bit.**
`resolving_the_leg_once_answers_what_resolving_it_every_time_answered` walks a
scheduled record round its whole day at 0.1 h steps with a non-zero `rephase_m`,
comparing `to_bits()` on the position and the re-phase and `ptr::eq` on the path
— an epsilon would admit different arithmetic, and *the same arithmetic in the
same order* is the claim. It cannot pass by comparing one leg 241 times (the
sweep must cross all four) and it walks an unscheduled record too.

**Measured on the island's own settled step**, which is where the 6.5× was
measured: `crowd` **0.353 → 0.208 ms** over the same derived residents — 1.07 µs
an agent to **0.63**, so the scheduled-against-walking ratio comes from 6.5× to
**3.9×**. On the sweep's own thousand walkers the phase reads **0.151 ms**
against NPC1d's 0.164 and NPC1c's 0.234.

### Lever 4 — character impostors, re-priced and refused a second time

The brief routes them *"for `Far` ONLY if the measurement demands them"*, and
NPC1b refused them with a sentence this wave was asked to re-check at the current
numbers: *"a `Far` agent already costs a share of one palette block, no group and
no draw."*

**Every term in that sentence got cheaper this wave, not dearer.** What a `Far`
agent costs the renderer today:

| what an impostor would replace | what it costs now |
|---|---|
| its own draw call | **none** — 1 001 skinned instances draw in **one** call per pass |
| its own joint palette | **a share of one block**: every `Far` agent of an archetype resolves to the same rest palette and `plan_skinned_batches` deduplicates it by `Arc` pointer |
| its own shadow group | **none, and now no shadow at all** — this wave's `casts_shadow` rung |
| its own GI contribution | **none** — this wave's per-instance pre-reject drops the whole instance before a joint is staged |
| GPU time | the whole skinned pass is **0.249–0.583 ms** for a thousand characters |

Against that, an impostor is an atlas, a bake, a cache, a per-frame card build
and a new asset kind — and it would not touch either of the two stations the
arc's own measurements say a crowd actually costs: the **fixed step** and the
**CPU-side projection and recording**. On the island the frame is CPU-bound by a
factor of two, so an hour spent on the GPU half buys a frame nothing.

**The measurement that would flip this ruling is stated rather than left open**: a
GPU-bound configuration in which `skinned-mesh` is a material share of the GPU
frame. It is not one today and the arc never produced one. Refused, for the
second time, with the numbers that refuse it.

### Lever 5 — the crowd's shadow LOD

NPC1b's carried item 4, and the NPC1b audit's item 13 under it. The proxy retired
`VSM_MAX_GROUPS` and did not touch the churn: 968 boxes walking through Harbour
City scattered page invalidation over **168.6 pages a frame against the island's
own 56.3**, at 1 236 page draws against 328 — and `deferred_pages` doubled with
them, so the crowd was also serving more *stale* shadow. One group is the right
answer to a group ceiling and no answer at all to how many pages a moving crowd
dirties. The item named the lever: *"proxies that stop casting past a radius."*

`CrowdTier::casts_shadow` is a **third rung** on the ladder, at the ladder's own
`Near` (96 m) rather than at a render setting, because the tier is the one place
a distance decision about a crowd is made and both projectors read it through
that door. `SkinnedShadow::None` is the renderer's side: no group, no proxy box,
no caster sphere, no palette slot, no page fold. **The cost is visible and is
stated** — past 96 m an NPC has no shadow, which is the same bargain `Proxy`
already struck one rung in.

`VsmRasterStats::shadow_lod_skipped` counts it, apart from `dropped_casters`,
because a ceiling firing is a defect and a shadow LOD firing is the feature
working.

**Measured on the island**, per rastering frame at N = 1 000:

| | NPC1b | **NPC1e** |
|---|---|---|
| pages, control → crowd | 56.3 → **168.6** (+112.3) | 59.3 → **101.7** (**+42.4**) |
| `vsm raster` CPU recording | 0.643 → 1.677 (+1.03) | ≈0.62 → **1.443** (+0.82) |
| proxy casters | 967 | **255** (the `Near` tier alone) |
| past the shadow LOD | — | **712** |

**The churn delta is 2.6× smaller** *(the NPC1e audit's arithmetic: the row's own
two numbers subtract to +42.4, not the +45.1 first published, and 112.3 / 42.4 is
2.65 — the claim was understated by its own typo).* What is left is the 255 `Near` agents, who
are inside 96 m and keep their shadow deliberately.

### THE CERTIFICATION — the island, at the hour its town is on the street

RTX 4070 Ti, Windows/Vulkan, **release**, **1080p**, the shipping `LIT+VIS`
stack, MIN of 3 rounds × 120 frames, the same 40 m flight east from Harbour City
that every island wave since I7b has flown. Both clocks the I8c ruling separates
are printed, and **p50 is the number**.

#### The N the island certifies at is ONE THOUSAND, and it is a ceiling

Nobody installs it. `inf_ecs::society::sync_society` derives a population from
the level's own buildings, and by the time the instrument reaches this row
**33 of Harbour City's blocks are resident and have offered 5 876 homes** — so
`SOCIETY_MAX_AGENTS = 1000` fires and **4 876 homes are declined and counted**.
NPC1d's arithmetic said a settlement of a hundred and seventy blocks implies
about fourteen thousand people; this is that sentence arriving as a measurement,
and the number the engine actually carries is the ceiling rather than the census.

#### The staging, and the row it replaced — 189 metres

The obvious placement for the hero is the settlement's own centre, which is
`island_gate`'s staging for the day gate. On this island the **authored player
start already is** Harbour City's centre — 0 m away — and measured from there:

> 33 volumes folded, 5 876 homes offered, 1 000 agents, 1 000 scheduled;
> **0 `Full` / 0 `Near` / 998 `Far` / 2 `Dormant`; 0 steering intents.**

A row taken there prices a town that **never enters the mover**, which is the one
system the whole arc named as its wall. A settlement's centre is its crossroads,
and its people are not at the crossroads. So the hero stands where the ladder's
own `Full` radius holds the most of them, which the instrument finds by asking:

> the town's centre is (−1750, 2050); the thickest part of its rush hour is
> (−1597, 2162), **189 m away**, with **191 residents inside a 32 m ring**. The
> hero's 998 materialized neighbours are **2 / 4 / 96 m** away (nearest, tenth,
> median).
>
> **170 `Full` / 335 `Near` / 493 `Far` / 2 `Dormant`; 170 steering intents,
> 112 blocked.**

One hundred and eighty-nine metres is the whole difference between a
certification and a vacuous one, and the row now asserts `Full > 0` so the
staging cannot drift back.

#### THE LAW THE CERTIFICATION FOUND

`character move` at **0.494 ms a character for 170 controllers** against
**0.171 at thirty-three** is three times a per-character cost that
`the_movers_cost_per_character_does_not_climb_with_the_crowd` holds **flat over a
64× range in N**, and that the NPC1c audit ruled *"genuinely linear"*. Both are
right, and they are about different variables.

**Neither existing arm sweeps density.**
`a_controller_pays_for_the_body_in_front_of_it_not_for_the_crowds_size` puts
**one** bystander two metres in front of each mover and then adds more of them
*further out*, so what it grows is the crowd's **extent** — and its 1.24×,
saturating between 64 and 256, is the correct answer to the question it asks. A
town's morning commute is not that shape: it is 191 bodies inside a 32 m ring,
and every one of them is inside somebody's sweep.

So the arc closes with the third question measured
(`the_movers_cost_is_flat_in_a_crowds_size_and_not_in_its_density`): 32
controllers, the same populations **spread over the 7 m lattice** and **packed
into the twenty metres the controllers stand in**.

| bystanders | spread | packed | |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 50.91 µs a character | 46.44 | 0.91× — the same world, and it must be |
| 64 | 58.09 | **91.83** | 1.58× |
| 192 | 62.23 | **159.39** | **2.56×** |
| 384 | 67.19 | **177.24** | 2.64× |

**2.6× per character for the same population**, which is the island's 2.9×
arriving on a fixture a tenth its size. The clocks are printed and the shape is
asserted, and the two anti-vacuity bounds differ on purpose because the
difference *is* the phenomenon: a body pressed into a rush hour covers **0.30 m**
where the spread arrangement takes it **1.56**, because the crowd is in its way.

**That is the arc's closing sentence about its own wall.** "0.18 ms a character"
was never a constant; it is a function of how many capsules are inside one
controller's sweep, and a crowd is exactly the content that makes that number
large. The levers the NPC1c audit named — *fewer or cheaper queries per
character* — are still the right ones, and this says which ones will pay: a
query that has to slide past two hundred capsules is not made cheaper by a
coarser ground probe.

### The ten walls, and where each one ended

The arc's brief opened with a scouted, file-line-verified list of ten walls. This
is their closing ledger: **dead**, **tripwired**, or **carried with a sentence** —
and where it is dead, the arm that would notice if it came back.

1. **THE TRACE** — `pose_state_bytes` is 36 + 40 B a joint, **6 476 B a posed
   character a step** at 161 bones, and `island_gate` retains every step's bytes;
   N = 1 000 × 900 steps is 5.8 GB in one test process. **DEAD, re-shaped, and
   tripwired.** A crowd section carries **58 B an agent at every tier** against a
   posed character's 6 476 — a **111×** per-agent ratio — and the tiers decide
   how many of a level's characters are on the pose path at all. Measured on the
   wave that finally put a population in front of it: NPC1d's day gate ran
   329 agents × 1 200 steps at **22 898 400 B** of crowd section, where 329 posed
   characters would have been **2.6 GB**. *And the wall the ledger did not
   predict is the one the instrument found*: at N = 100 NPC1a measured the trace
   growing 1 118 B an agent of which the **deformation field was 752** and the
   pose 251. *(The NPC1e audit re-ran the sweep at this head: it is now **479 B
   an agent — crowd 58 + snapshot 67 + pose 251 + deform 104** — because NPC1c
   gave the tier the components and a `Far` agent presses no ground. The field is
   no longer the dominant section at the banded tiers; see the corrected carried
   item below, and note that NPC1a's own 752-of-1 118 was printed as "63 %" when
   the division is 67 %.)* Tripwires: `inf_ecs::crowd`'s
   `…_fifty_eight_bytes`, and `island_gate`'s drive arm, which pins the pose
   store as a **multiple** of 6 476 with a **count** bound of `1 + society.agents`
   — so neither a rig that shrank nor a town that grew can hide in it.

2. **STREAMED NPCS GET NO BRAIN** — the Blueprint actor map is fixed at
   `RuntimeSim` construction, and an entity that WALKS two cells over is deleted
   when its birth cell deactivates. **HALF DEAD, HALF DECIDED.** The despawn is
   fixed: `sync_sim` re-homes a walked-away entity into the cell it is standing
   in and counts it (`CellStreamStats::rehomed`), with the conservative half
   untouched, a returning-birth-cell arm the NPC1a audit added after measuring
   **two entities carrying one `Guid`**, and `rehomed == 0` on the island because
   the island's own content stands still. The actor map is **deliberately not
   opened**, and the deferral's sentence now says why rather than only that: a
   `Tick` blueprint writing one variable is **0.494 µs** an actor against a crowd
   agent's **0.081** — 6.1×, re-measured by the audit at 5.7× — so 1 000 of them
   is 8.2 % of a 6.0 ms step before an NPC has thought about anything.
   **Carried:** the general `spawn_with_guid` refusal, which `crowd::add_agents`
   now has for its own caller and which every other spawner in the engine still
   does not.

3. **ONE DRAW + ONE BIND GROUP + ONE 16 KiB PALETTE PER CHARACTER ×2** —
   instanced skinning was "the documented P15 optimization", unbuilt for eleven
   phases. **DEAD.** One draw per mesh per pass (2 a frame against 2 002), the
   palette atlas deduplicated by `Arc` pointer, and the joint block packed into
   two vertex channels that were zero since P7.1 — the first use of
   `p26-5-vertex-streams.md`'s channel-packing route past a full 16/16 attribute
   set. On the island's own 161-bone hero: **31.3 MB a frame → 3.33 MB, 9.4×**.
   Tripwires: `plan_skinned_batches`' six arms, both stores'
   `the_shared_palette_is_the_one_the_per_agent_path_would_have_built`, and the
   NPC1b audit's `the_atlas_is_filled_once_per_block_and_matches_the_per_instance_fill`.
   **Carried:** the third of the three things P15 named — a **GPU palette compute
   pass** — which is the lever for the projection's `+2.86 ms`, and which needs
   the pose to reach the renderer as data rather than as a finished palette.

4. **`VSM_MAX_GROUPS` = 1 024 AND A SKINNED INSTANCE IS ONE GROUP** — past it a
   crowd's shadows are refused. **DEAD TWICE OVER.** NPC1b's shared proxy group
   took the island's crowd to **35 groups of 1 024, 0 dropped, 0 refused** over
   478 rastering frames — it would take about **thirty-two thousand NPCs at that
   banded ratio** to reach the ceiling, which is a thousand `Full` ones, since a
   `Full` agent is exactly one group *(the NPC1e audit corrected this sentence:
   it read "thirty-two thousand `Full` NPCs", which is the ceiling times
   thirty-two)* — and this wave took the half the proxy left standing: past `Near`
   an agent casts **nothing at all**. The sweep's own closing table is the wall
   in two numbers: **35 groups banded against 1 001 all-`Full`**. Tripwires:
   `a_crowd_of_proxies_is_one_group_and_refuses_nothing` (1 030 instances,
   `dropped_groups` 11 a frame → 0) and this wave's
   `a_crowd_past_the_shadow_lod_casts_nothing_and_dirties_fewer_pages`.
   `SKINNED_POSE_MARGIN` is retired for the instances that ask (the exact posed
   union bound, **67 % of the radius and 30 % of the volume** on its own
   fixture), and the "posed AABB `inf-anim` is still not handed" turned out to be
   a forward reference to a bound the renderer already held both halves of.

5. **ZERO ANIM LOD** — the full pose pipeline per `AnimStateMachine` entity per
   fixed step regardless of distance. **DEAD.** The ladder is the LOD and it keys
   on **sim** state (`StreamingSource` distance on the `SimBand` lattice), never
   on a camera — `step_crowd` has no camera argument, so a caller cannot pass one
   by accident. Measured at N = 1 000 against an all-`Full` control, and the arc's
   closing sweep is a **bigger** number than NPC1a's because NPC1c gave `Full` a
   controller and the control is now a thousand movers inside each other's
   sweeps: the whole fixed step is **7.697 ms banded against 153.784 all-`Full`,
   20.0×** (NPC1a's was 2.0×), the `animation` phase **1.112 against 5.101,
   4.59×** (NPC1a's 3.5×), and the trace **450 713 B against 2 983 476, 6.6×**
   (NPC1a's 3.0×). Tripwire: the sweep's banded/all-`Full`
   control pair and `island_gate`'s `posed == hero + Full + Near` equality, which
   the NPC1a audit re-wrote after measuring that the old `posed < N + 1` clause
   was satisfied by the `Dormant` count alone. **Carried:** the `Near` rung still
   saves nothing a test can see — `hand_ik()` gates `hand_requests`, which is
   composed over entities carrying `CharacterMovement`, and a `Near` agent has
   none.

6. **THE FIXED STEP HAS NO ROOM** — 5.67–5.85 of a 6.0 ms ratchet before an NPC
   existed, and no NPC budget anywhere. **CARRIED, and it is the arc's
   remainder.** The crowd got its own phases (`STEP_PHASES` 24 → 26, `crowd` and
   `society`) and its own budgets, and on the island as a player boots it they
   hold with room: the isolated step reads `crowd` **0.208 ms** against
   `NPC_STEP_BUDGET_MS` 1.0 and `society` **0.167** against
   `SOCIETY_STEP_BUDGET_MS` 0.5, in a step of **6.571 ms** against NPC1d's 7.930.
   **At the certification station `crowd` reads 1.125 and the budget is exceeded
   for the first time in the arc** — 1 000 scheduled agents of which 170 steer,
   and a steered agent's pursuit projects its body onto its own path. It is
   **carried rather than re-minted**, because a budget that moves the day it is
   exceeded is a report.
   And the wall's own sentence is unchanged and is the arc's remainder: **the
   crowd's cost is not in the crowd's phases.** At the certification station the
   crowd's own two phases are 1.4 of 118.6 ms; the rest is `character move`,
   `gameplay`, `animation`, `physics3d sync`, the `solver` and `terrain stream`
   — six systems the crowd is a *customer* of rather than the author of.

7. **BLUEPRINT TICK IS SERIAL** — host construction plus a map remove/insert per
   actor per step. **DECIDED WITH A NUMBER**, and the number is wall 2's. Crowd
   brains are a dedicated system on plain data; Blueprint is reserved for
   hero-class actors; the deferral stands with its price written down.
   `parallel_map` was measured before it was prescribed and **pays nowhere**
   between N = 1 and N = 10 000 (0.02× to 0.36×), so none of it was wired and the
   table that says why is in the instrument.

8. **NO NAV — BUT THE GRAPHS EXIST.** **DEAD.** `inf-nav` is Ring 0, `glam` and
   nothing else, no new external crate and no schema; three producers expose
   themselves (`RoadGraph::nav_graph`, `BuildingPlan::room_path`/`interior_nav`,
   `Settlement::street_graph` — 459 nodes / 1 320 directed edges over seven
   settlements); `NavVerdict` is a value with three named refusals; ties break on
   the node id; an edge carries its own spine. NPC1d added the level network the
   *cooked pack* can build — pavement rings round the blocks and each building's
   own front door — and the **two-level search**, which is a measurement rather
   than a taste: one graph with every interior in it is ~25 000 nodes and ~11 ms
   a search. Tripwires: `pie_equals_shipping_when_an_npc_walks_across_town`
   (6 480 steps, 6 480 distinct, identical on both hosts, three doors opened,
   89 % of a staircase climbed) and
   `a_town_sized_grid_is_searched_within_dijkstras_own_bounds`, which counts
   Dijkstra's own work after the CI-red taught this arc that a structural claim
   fitting in a counter must never be spent on a clock.

9. **THE COLLIDER BAND** — NPCs as anchors is an explosion, NPCs as non-anchors
   walk through un-collided buildings. **DEAD AS DESIGNED**, and the resolution
   is the tier: `Far` is kinematic-on-the-graph with no rapier body, `Full` and
   `Near` are solid. NPC1c made the tier own the **components** rather than have
   the bridge decline to mirror them, which is what closed the door NPC1a had
   left ajar (a thousand `Far` agents were a thousand *terrain observers*).
   Tripwires: `a_banded_out_crowd_agent_gets_no_rapier_body` (a `Full` agent with
   one, a `Far` one without, **and the transition**),
   `only_the_crowd_tiers_with_a_body_observe_the_terrain`,
   `a_crowd_agent_with_no_body_presses_no_ground`, and
   `a_narrowed_capsule_computes_no_manifold_against_a_far_buildings_shell`.

10. **THE TEN NOS** — no persistence, no pooling, no impostor characters, no
    seats, no per-NPC lights, no free vertex attribute. **One dead, one refused
    with a measurement, the rest carried by name.** The vertex attribute is
    **dead**: channel packing is built and is the first consumer of
    `p26-5-vertex-streams.md`. **Character impostors are refused for the second
    time**, and the re-pricing is below. Persistence, pooling, `SitPoint`, seats,
    `Talk`'s first consumer and per-NPC lights are **not built**; each is carried
    with the reason, and the two the brief called *"if cheap"* were measured not
    to be — an affordance a body uses is a second authority over where that body
    is, which is exactly what the schedule's one-position law exists to avoid.

Every arm the arc built, re-run on this tree after four behavioural changes to
the mover, the crowd step, the GI staging path and the shadow map:

| the gate | what it holds | at head |
|---|---|---|

**Nothing in this wave moved a trace**, and the reason is structural rather than
lucky: the mover's probe feeds `slide_friction` and nothing else, so a character
that never slides reads the same `+Y` it would have measured on flat ground; the
leg is resolved once and answers the same bits; and `SkinnedShadow` and
`GiAudit` are render-side types that no serialized format and no trace section
has ever seen.
### The laws this wave paid for

* **An anti-vacuity clause has to know what it is ruling out.** The NPC1c audit's
  four-world table asked `travelled_m > 1.0` and got it from a body that fell a
  hundred and forty metres. "The character moved" and "the character walked" are
  different claims, and the whole arc's mover lever was aimed with a table that
  compared one against the other.
* **Price the primitive, not the phase.** *"Four heightfield tiles cost more than
  1 849 buildings"* is a 1.3× at the phase and an **11.3×** at the cast, and only
  the second number tells you what to do about it. A phase is a sum over
  programs; a primitive is a thing you can delete one of.
  *(Corrected by the NPC1e audit: this law was first written with a **75×** taken
  from a probe that hit nothing — see the correction box under the lever's table.
  The law survives its own arithmetic; the number in it did not, and the audit's
  own restatement is the third bullet below.)*
* **A ratio is only a ratio if both halves hit.** The correction above is this
  wave's own anti-vacuity law applied to the wave: it caught a free-falling body
  inside somebody else's table and then priced a primitive against a broad phase
  saying "no" in its own. `where_the_movers_queries_go` now asserts that the
  probe hits exactly on the worlds with ground under the character, and that the
  ray reaches what the sphere reaches — two clauses that cost nothing and would
  have refused both defects on the day they were written.
* **A field that only one branch reads is a query nobody else should pay for.**
  `ground_normal` is written every step by every grounded character in the engine
  and read by `slide_friction` alone. Grepping the *reader* is what turned an 18 %
  cost into a predicate.
* **A conservative bound is only worth having if it is tight enough to reject
  something.** The GI pre-reject needed two arms pointing opposite ways: one that
  fails when the bound is too small (it would drop a box the volume kept) and one
  that fails when it is too large (an NPC five metres past the face must still be
  rejected). Either alone is satisfiable by a bound that says "everything".
* **A gate staged where a defect cannot appear is a gate that certifies the
  defect** — NPC1d's own law, met by the wave that quoted it. The certification
  row's first cut stood the hero at the level's authored player start, and from
  there **every one of the island's residents is `Far`**: 0 `Full`, 0 `Near`,
  0 steering intents, and a row that would have certified a town which never
  enters the mover — the one system the whole arc named as its wall.
* **A one-way door decides an instrument's ORDER.** `set_crowd_population` marks
  the population hand-installed and the society stops deriving, so the derived-
  society row cannot follow a hand-installed one. The row list is ordered by that
  fact and says so, rather than by what reads nicely.
* **`rustfmt` and a scripted edit will eat a `\`-continuation, still.** Three
  more this wave, in three different files, every one caught by the workspace
  gate the P22 law paid for. The remedy remains the one NPC1a wrote down: a
  print's visual indentation belongs *outside* the string, and a literal written
  by a script gets read back before it is believed.
* **An arm can be right about its variable and wrong about the world.**
  *"A controller pays for the body in front of it, not for the crowd's size"* is
  a true sentence about a fixture that adds bystanders **outward**, and it read
  as a general statement about crowds for two waves. The island's rush hour adds
  them **inward**, and the same mover costs 2.6× per character. The tell is that
  the arm's own knob and the content's own knob are not the same quantity.
* **A budget exceeded is a station to name, not a number to re-mint.**
  `NPC_STEP_BUDGET_MS` is over for the first time in the arc, at 1.125 against
  1.0, and moving it would convert a measurement into a report.

   overwhelmingly other NPCs, and a crowd's own separation is a steering problem
   rather than a swept-shape one. The blocker is that the mover has no per-caller
   collider filter, and that "NPCs walk through each other" is a product

## Wave NPC1e — the adversarial audit (2026-08-28)

Range `077698d9..adce89ce`, seven commits, **already pushed** — the implementer
breached the push ban and CI is running on the wave. Fixes land as follow-up
commits. The battery was re-run at head before a line was touched: **green,
0 failed**.

**The wave's four levers all do what they say.** The mover asks the world once
(`queries` 2.00 → 1.00, mutation-verified: forcing the predicate `true` kills
exactly one arm and no other), the GI pre-reject is sound in both directions and
memoized on a genuinely call-local map, the leg is resolved once and the
arithmetic is unchanged, and the shadow LOD is a whole drop counted apart from a
refusal. The density law **reproduces on this machine**. What the audit found is
in the *reasoning around* the levers rather than in the levers: **two of the
wave's own laws were broken by the wave in the act of writing them**, and one
carried item has been stale for four ledgers.

### HIGH — the primitive table divided a HIT by a MISS, and it became a law

Lever 1's table published the section-9 probe at **5.6 µs** against *"the same
probe against 1 849 building boxes"* at **0.07**, called it **~75× per cast**,
and spent that number three times: as the sentence that *"four heightfield tiles
cost more than 1 849 buildings"* is *"much stronger than it was published as"*,
as the closing law **"price the primitive, not the phase — 1.3× at the phase and
75× at the cast"**, and as carried item 1(b)'s prescription *"take the terrain
out of a crowd agent's mover queries — the height-field cast costs 75× what a
building cast does"*.

The 0.07 row is the fixture's `ground(false)` world. **Its character has been in
free fall since the settle loop** — the same body this wave corrected the
four-world table for, one function above in the same file, in the same commit —
so it stands at **y = −1.334 m** under a box field whose lowest face is y = 0,
and its probe **hits nothing at all**. 0.07 µs is a broad phase saying "no".

The **ray at 0.18 µs** was worse in two ways. `character_move_cost.rs` contained
**no ray measurement anywhere** in the range (`grep -n "cast_ray"` over the file:
nothing), so a row of a table introduced with *"priced one at a time … in
`character_move_cost::where_the_movers_queries_go`"* came from no arm at all —
this repository's *"a cited gate that doesn't exist is worse than no claim"*. And
a ray of `probe_len` from the capsule's centre stops **above** the ground the
probe sphere's own radius reaches, so it answers `None` for free: re-measured at
that reach it reads 0.18 µs in the fixture and **misses**.

**Fixed** (`d55cd088`), with the clause `what_a_cast_against_the_ground_costs`
already carried three functions away and this arm did not: `probe_hit` is
asserted equal to the world's own `ground` flag and `ray_hit` equal to
`probe_hit`, so a row that found nothing can never be quoted beside one that did;
a **box control** drops the identical probe onto a building's **roof** in the
same world, the same tree and the same filter; and the ray is measured to the
depth the sphere reaches. The slab `what_a_cast_against_the_ground_costs` already
built and never compared is now ratioed.

**Measured at head — every figure a hit:**

| in the mover's own fixture world (1 854 bodies) | µs |
|---|---|
| `move_character` | 25.8 |
| the section-9 probe into the **height field** | **5.62** |
| the same probe onto a building **roof** (a box) | **0.50** |
| the same depth as a downward **ray** | **0.25** |
| *(the old "against 1 849 boxes" row, which **misses**)* | *0.07* |

| the isolated one-body controls | µs |
|---|---|
| one 257-sample **tile** | 1.034 |
| one 512 × 512 m **box slab** | 0.356 |

So the ratio is **11.3× in the mover's own world and 2.9× on the isolated
control** — an order of magnitude, not seventy-five — and the law survives with
its arithmetic replaced. **And the audit's own addition to the carried levers:
the SHAPE of the cast is a bigger lever than the number of them.** A ray to the
same depth answers the same ground **22× cheaper in the fixture and 45× on the
ground-only world**, and the number it would replace has exactly one reader
(`slide_friction`'s slope). That is carried as item 1(b′).

**The lever itself is untouched and still pays**: the probe is 17.9 % of a step,
and the mutation (`reads_the_ground_normal` forced `true`) kills
`a_walking_character_asks_the_world_once_and_a_sprinting_one_twice` at walking
**2 against 1** and nothing else — one arm, which is what an armed lever looks
like.

### MED — the correction stopped at the wave that made it

The wave states *"the table the arc aimed with is CORRECTED"*, and the code is:
`Measured` carries `grounded`, `end_y` and queries-per-character-step and asserts
the shape both ways. **The NPC1c audit's ledger is not.** `adce89ce` is 781
insertions and **zero deletions** — the four-world table under *"Wave NPC1c — the
adversarial audit"* still reads as four ablations of one program, still says

heightfield tiles cost more than 1 849 buildings"* with nothing beside it. A
reader who lands there — which is where the whole arc's mover lever was aimed

**Fixed:** a correction box in place under that table, naming the free fall, the
y = −139.056, the 3.00-against-1.00 queries, and the corrected primitive ratio.

### MED — an equality arm that cannot fail, and a ledger that says it can

`resolving_the_leg_once_answers_what_resolving_it_every_time_answered` compares
`position_on(rec.leg_at(g, c), g, c)` against `position_at(g, c)`. After the
refactor `position_at` **is** `position_on(self.leg_at(g, c), …)`, and the same
holds for `progress_at`, `path_at` and `rephase_delta_at`. Every pair in the
241-step sweep is one expression evaluated twice, so the arm fails only if
`leg_at` stops being a pure function of its arguments — and the ledger's *"It is
not a tautology … the day somebody changes one of the pair the two answers part
company here"* is true only for a re-write that stops delegating, which is
precisely what the refactor removed.

The claim the refactor really makes is the one underneath: **the leg cannot
change inside a step**. That is falsifiable, because `step_crowd_banded` writes
two record fields between the single resolution and the last three sites that
read it — `rec.leg` in the leg-change check, `rec.rephase_m` in the demotion
re-phase.

**Fixed** (`f231cf0c`): the arm now also asserts that `leg_at` answers the same
thing across those writes at six hours of the day, and the doc says which half is
worth what. **Mutation-verified:** folding `self.leg` and `self.rephase_m` into
`hour_of`'s argument at 1e-9 fails the new half at 9.25 h and is **invisible to
the old one**.

**Fixed:** the item is rewritten with the measurement, the retiring wave and the

### MED — "it was not met at N = 0" is hung on a row with a thousand NPCs in it

The headline cites the plain `LIT+VIS` row at **25.319 ms** as the island alone

already labels *"the island, flown over, no crowd"*.

**The conclusion is unaffected** — both rows miss 60 fps and the ledger's
three-row subtraction is internally sound — but the sentence is hung on the wrong
number. **Fixed** in the memo and in ROADMAP §12.

### MED — the certification row's staging comment describes a staging nobody did

The row's block comment reads *"it stands the hero at its largest settlement's
centre, which is `island_gate`'s own staging for the day gate"*. The code does
none of the three: `island_town_centre` picks the **nearest** settlement (its own
doc explains why — the largest is 3.8 km off the flight, and residency follows
the streaming anchor rather than the camera), the centre is only ever
**reported**, and the hero is placed at **the thickest part of the rush hour**.
Since the 189 m between those two placements *is* this wave's staging finding, a
comment naming the vacuous one is the worst place in the file for a stale
sentence. **Fixed** (`f231cf0c`).

### MED — the +21.0 ms attributed to the collider band has no counter on the row it is about

The wave attributes **+21.0 ms of p50** for standing in the town to *"the town's
own admitted structure colliders"*. The phase split behind it is measured
(`physics3d sync` 6.487, `solver` 6.103, out of a fixed step that goes
6.976 → 14.653); **which bodies did it is not**. The island prints its body /
admitted-structure / contact-pair census exactly **once**, in the isolated
fixed-step block, at the hero's *authored start* — 189 m from the row the claim
is about — and `print_step_clocks` carries no census at all. This is the item the
wave routes to VEH1/I9, so the next wave inherits a mechanism nobody counted.

**Fixed** (`f231cf0c`): the census now prints per row, so the next run of the
instrument turns the attribution into a subtraction between two adjacent rows.
Until that run it is a mechanism, and the item says so.

### MED — wall 4's ceiling arithmetic is off by the ceiling

*"It would take thirty-two thousand `Full` NPCs to reach the ceiling"* — a `Full`
agent is **exactly one group** by construction (`pack_casters` pushes one
`GroupGeom` per non-proxy, non-`None` skinned instance), so **1 024** `Full` NPCs
reach `VSM_MAX_GROUPS`. Thirty-two thousand is the number of *NPCs at the
island's banded ratio* (33 `Full` per 1 000). **Fixed** in place; the wall's
disposition is unchanged.

### THE BUDGET RULING — carrying is legal; the staging is not

`NPC_STEP_BUDGET_MS` is exceeded for the first time in the arc, at **1.125
against 1.0**, and the wave carries it rather than re-minting it.

**§8's rule is a direction rule** — *"a hard ms budget … that only ratchets
down"* — so the thing it forbids is **raising** the constant. Refusing to move it
is not merely allowed, it is the required behaviour, and the wave's sentence *"a
budget that moves the day it is exceeded is a report"* is the doctrine correctly
applied. **The wave owes no red on this.**

What it does owe is a **staging**, and this is the finding. `crowd_sweep`'s
budget arm — the only place `NPC_STEP_BUDGET_MS` is asserted, in `--release` off
CI — measures **1 000 unscheduled ping-pong walkers, none of which steer**, and
reads **0.15 ms**. That is the one configuration in this tree that *cannot*
produce the 1.125: the ledger's own mechanism for the overrun is that *"a steered
agent's pursuit projects its body onto its own path"*. So the budget's gate is
staged where its defect cannot appear — **NPC1d's law applied to a ratchet
instead of to a certification**, by the wave that quoted that law twice.

**Ruling: re-stage, never re-mint.** The arm the next wave owes is the same sweep
row over a **scheduled, steering** population, reported first and asserted once
the station is understood. Routed on carried item 13; not built here, because
changing what a ratchet is asserted against is a wave's decision and not an
audit's.

### The density law — VERDICT: it reproduces, and the arm is honest

Re-run on this machine
(`the_movers_cost_is_flat_in_a_crowds_size_and_not_in_its_density`):

| bystanders | spread µs/char | packed µs/char | ratio | the ledger's |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 46.84 | 49.50 | 1.06× | 0.91× |
| 64 | 56.68 | 91.46 | 1.61× | 1.58× |
| 192 | 60.54 | 158.70 | **2.62×** | 2.56× |
| 384 | 67.20 | 177.98 | 2.65× | 2.64× |

**The law holds and the numbers are within run-to-run noise of the published
ones.** The zero-bystander row is the same world twice and lands either side of
1.00 on different runs, which is what the ledger says it must. *"0.18 ms a
character"* is correctly retired as a constant.

One honest bound on the fixture, carried rather than fixed: `agent_home` wraps at
`i % 289`, so the **spread** arrangement past 289 bystanders stacks the extras on
top of the first 95 sites rather than spreading further. It biases the spread row
**dearer**, so the measured ratio is if anything conservative — but "spread over
the 7 m lattice" is not exactly what the fixture builds at 384.

1. **NPC1a's trace decomposition prints its shares against a denominator it does

4. **`pack_casters`' `VSM_MAX_CASTERS` early break counts every remaining

5. **`gi::skinned_model_bound` sums SIGNED half-extents** where the staging

6. **The `dev`-profile clocks in `where_the_movers_queries_go` disagree with

7. **The tier census and the render census are read at different moments and are

## Wave VEH1a — the car drives the island (2026-08-28)

Base `3b466575`. Five clauses, all five taken. Wave I7 shipped 33.74 km of
graded, audited road and wrote two open items against it — *"the circuit is
drawn and audited, and nothing drives it"* and *"the road network's topology is
asserted on a flat fixture"* — and this wave closes both, with a car that is
simulated rather than scripted and a walk over the graph the road builder
actually builds.

> **The island has a fleet, and the fleet drives.** Seven settlements, seven
> cars, **38 drawn body parts and no new committed file**; the hero enters
> through the seat door the phase-29 rig already had and covers **34.1 m in 300
> steps at up to 16.81 m/s, byte-identical on both hosts**; the catalogue's
> 1 185 kg sedan climbs the **0.108** grade I7's own audit found and tops out at
> **26.19 m/s (94 km/h)** doing it; and **every one of Vancouver Island's 42
> ordered site pairs is reachable** over the built `RoadGraph`.

### Clause 1 — the D-14 surface, and the two things it turned out to be

P29.7 left two facts about a wheel on real ground written down and unmeasured.
Both are now numbers, and **neither disposition is the one the brief expected**.

**THE NORMAL SNAP IS REAL AND IT REACHES NO FORCE.** `FIX_INTERNAL_EDGES` is on
every heightfield this engine builds and it fixes *contacts*; a ray reads the
hit triangle's own normal, un-fixed, so a wheel crossing a cell diagonal sees
that vector jump. Measured over 800 five-centimetre steps of a 45° walk across
40 cells of a 1 m lattice — the island's own grid:

| surface | worst normal step | steps over 1° | worst height step |
|---|---|---|---|
| the levelled road corridor (a smooth 0.108 cross-slope) | **0.0643°** | 0 of 800 | 0.006240 m |
| open ground (0.15 m of per-sample DTM relief) | **15.6898°** | **74 of 800** | 0.014408 m |

The height is continuous and the normal is not, which is exactly what C0-and-not-C1
looks like. The routed repair — **wheel-side normal smoothing** — is **refused**,
and refused with a falsifier rather than an argument: `RaycastVehicle::solve`
pushes its suspension along the **chassis up** (deliberately, since projecting
onto the contact normal is how a car slides sideways off a ramp it should drive
up) and takes its friction basis from the steered wheel's own axes, so no force
is a function of that vector. Two rigs were driven 600 steps across the rough
surface, one of them with **every contact normal replaced by a direction the
ground could not have**, and they end **bit-identical** — 0.000000 m apart, over
1 860 wheel contacts of a possible 2 400 and 61.72 m of travel.
`the_snapped_normal_reaches_no_force_in_the_model` is that arm, and it goes red
the day an island class starts reading the field.

**THE SENSOR RIDE IS CLOSED**, as the P29.7 ledger asked it to be — *"a
query-layer decision with its own arms, not a vehicle-wave footnote"*.
`CastTargets::AllSolid` is the third variant (every body kind, sensors excluded,
through rapier's own filter flags so the rejection happens as the tree is walked
and the ground beneath a trigger is still found); the wheel ray is its only
caller. Measured: with a sensor slab under all four wheels the car settles
**0.9617 m** over the ground against its springs' 0.9529, and **the same slab as
a solid holds it 0.8 m higher** — so the arm is about the sensor flag and not
about a collider the bridge failed to mirror.

Three more numbers the clause asked for, reported rather than repaired:

* **the ray and `height_at` are one surface to 0.039784 m** at 0.15 m of relief,
  over 300 probes — the twist inside a cell, triangulation against bilinear. On
  the levelled corridor the road's own cross-section error is the I2 audit's
  measured **0.000750 m**, so the "≤ 5 cm" bound is dominated by open ground and
  not by the circuit;
* **the sink is the lift**: the road ribbon is drawn at `DEFAULT_ROAD_LIFT_M`
  = 0.02 m above the heightfield the wheels are cast into (roads carry no
  colliders — IB-4's priced ruling), so a wheel rides two centimetres under the
  visible tarmac at every ribbon vertex;
* **at speed the ride is the suspension's**: at 24.00 m/s the chassis departs its
  settled 0.9614 m clearance by **0.0517 m**, inside its own 0.25 m of travel,
  and never comes within its half-height of the ground.

And one the fixture found on its own: **a car parked on a 0.108 grade rolls
4.5763 m in two seconds** with nothing applied, and 0.0554 m on the handbrake.
P29.7's `a_parked_rig_settles_on_its_springs_and_stays_there` is on a box floor,
where "stays there" is free.

### Clause 2 — the car gets a body, and the body it had was sideways

**THE FINDING IS WAVE I8b's, WEARING A BUMPER.** The committed car draws
`Primitive::Cube` on a `Transform` with **scale one** over a collider of eight
cubic metres — a one-metre cube standing in for a car, which is precisely what
I8b found the settlements doing. And underneath it, invisible *because* of it:
`PHASE29_CAR_HALF` is `(2.0, 0.5, 1.0)` and `+Z` is forward in this engine, so
the phase-29 course's car is **four metres wide and two long**, standing across a
1.8 m track on a 2.8 m wheelbase. Its own doc calls it "4 × 1 × 2 m", which it
is — in the order width, height, length.

That one is **not fixed** (that `.inf_lvl` has a twenty-arm gate over it and
re-proportioning the chassis moves every number in it) and it is **asserted**:
`the_phase29_courses_car_is_still_wider_than_it_is_long` goes red the day
somebody fixes it and names the ledger item that owed it.

**The body.** `inf_ecs::vehicle::VehicleBody` is two silhouettes as unions of
axis-aligned boxes in **fractions of the hull** — the I8b proportional-module
lesson one content kind over, so one table serves a saloon and a pickup at any
size — with content-derived part GUIDs (`body_part_guid`, the synthetic-guid rule
this repo already uses for door leaves, doorways, structure colliders, fracture
chunks and building modules) and **no committed mesh file**. Axis-aligned boxes
and one cylinder, because `inf-dcc` refuses a bevel on edges that share an
endpoint (the P23 finding) and a car body is nothing but such edges.

| family | parts | what they are |
|---|---|---|
| `Sedan` | 4 | lower body, set-back greenhouse, bonnet, boot |
| `Truck` | 6 | lower body, tall cab, bed floor, two bed sides, headboard |

Every part is asserted inside the hull it is drawn on, filling it on all three
axes, leaving real air in it, and with a **roof narrower and much shorter than
the hull** — the clause that separates a silhouette from a brick drawn in six
pieces.

**Why not the scatter path.** The brief routed the I8b module-mesh route, and the
batch type refuses it in its own words: `ScatterData::key` is a content hash over
the *instance records*, and a vehicle's instances carry its rotation, so a moving
car re-keys its batch every frame — the one thing the anchor being outside the
key exists to prevent. The parts are ordinary scene entities drawing built-in
primitives, which costs the projectors nothing and needs no table either host
could drift on. What is borrowed from I8b is the part that mattered: proportional
families, content-derived ids, no committed bytes.

**The wheels get tyres, and the tyre is a grandchild.** `step_vehicles` writes
the wheel entity's rotation every step as euler `(spin, steer, 0)` — there is no
roll slot left to lay a `+Y`-axis cylinder down with — so the tyre is a child of
the wheel whose local transform is authored once and never written.

**The catalogue is TOML with ZERO schema**, on the `WeaponDef` /
`GAMEPLAY_ITEMS_TOML` precedent: `VehicleDef` derives no `Serialize`, the table
is a `&str` this crate reads at **generation** time, and what reaches the level is
a chassis, four sensor wheels, a body and the `VehicleClass` the scene has carried
since v25. `VehicleClass` grew a `set`/`to_tuning` pair that routes through
`VehicleTuning::names()` rather than restating it, so a tuning name added to the
door reaches an authored row on the day it is added.

| row | body | mass | top speed |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sedan` | 1.84 × 1.24 × **4.40 m** | 1 185 kg | 122 km/h |
| `truck` | 2.04 × 1.64 × **5.30 m** | 2 341 kg | 97 km/h |

**The island spawns them** — one at the nearest *planned route vertex* to each
settlement, which is where the drivable circuit passes the town and the only
place on this island a **committed** number says what the ground height is
(`inf_island::nearest_route_vertex`, which `player_start` now shares). Nothing
here reads an elevation, so the level stays authorable without the terrain, and
the yaw is `patan2_64` because it is serialized. Not `AlwaysLoaded`: a car streams
with its partition cell exactly as a settlement block does.

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `VancouverIsland.inf_lvl` | 49 625 B | **73 633 B** — 7 cars, 38 drawn body parts |
| `IslandFixture.inf_lvl` | 9 990 B | **16 671 B** — 2 cars, 10 drawn body parts |
| committed files | — | **unchanged**: no `.inf_mesh`, no new asset kind |

### Clause 3 — the vehicle phase

`STEP_PHASES` **26 → 27**. `vehicle` is index 12, immediately after
`character move`, which is exactly where `step_vehicles` has always run — the
ordering is untouched and no trace moved. What moved is that the milliseconds are
attributed. Every constant below it shifts by one and both pins that name them
(`the_names_and_the_indices_are_one_table`,
`the_phase_indices_are_a_permutation_of_the_slots`) move with it.

**THE TRADE IS STATED AND PAID FOR.** P29.7 put the call inside
`step_character_movement`'s last statement on a real argument — *"a sibling both
hosts had to call separately would be a hand-maintained mirror"* — and the price
was a phase that cannot say where its milliseconds went, which is the defect wave
I4b exists to remove. So the mirror is **paid for rather than avoided**:
`inf-editor-core/tests/fixed_step_mirror.rs` pins the two call sites
character-for-character through the same fence instrument the projectors use,
pins their **order** on both hosts (mover < vehicle < gameplay < solver — a
vehicle step after the solver applies forces the solver has already integrated
past), and pins that the movement door does not still step them itself, which an
equality fence in two files cannot see. That is a *stronger* guard than the
arrangement it replaces, which pinned the call and left nothing at all pinning
the two hosts agreeing about **when**.

**The budget is minted from a measurement.** `the_vehicle_phase_asks_four_
questions_a_car_and_costs_what_it_prints` asserts the **count** a clock cannot
see — the phase asks the world exactly four questions a car a step, one ray a
wheel — and reports the clock:

| cars | dev | release | per car (dev) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 0.0015 ms | 0.0012 | 1.51 µs |
| 4 | 0.0053 | 0.0041 | 1.33 |
| 16 | 0.0227 | 0.0178 | 1.42 |
| **64** | **0.1101 ms** | **0.0882** | **1.72 µs** |

`VEHICLE_STEP_BUDGET_MS = 0.5` at `VEHICLE_BUDGET_CARS = 64` — ~4.5× the dev
measurement, deliberately tighter than `NPC_STEP_BUDGET_MS`'s ten-fold because
four casts a car have nothing that is *supposed* to vary, and a twelfth of
`CITY_STEP_BUDGET_MS`, which is what makes it able to see anything. §8
direction-only.

**The engine audio adds no audio API.** `Vehicle::engine_state` answers two
numbers in `[0, 1]` — revs and load — with a default of **silence**, so a class
that has not thought about sound makes none; `engine_cue` maps them onto pitch and
volume in Ring 0, clamping and refusing non-finites so no NaN reaches a mixer;
each host's audio step spends them as the P12.3 `Play`/`SetPitch`/`SetVolume`
that have existed since phase 12. The cue is read off **this step's published
`VehicleOutcome`** rather than off the vehicle map, so the stream stays a pure
function of sim state — the P12 doctrine, met by a system that moves. Fenced and
pinned in both hosts, with a refusal clause: the loop may not reach for a command
the queue does not have.

### Clause 4 — the gate

**THE DRIVE.** `pie_equals_shipping_when_the_car_drives_the_circuit` is
`pie_equals_shipping_on_an_island_drive` with the scripted 0.8 m/step teleport
replaced by a car. The hero is stood beside the settlement's own vehicle, presses
`INTERACT` through the shipped seat door (the same `interact::resolve` a doorway
is ranked by), and holds the throttle; from there nothing is teleported, so the
`StreamingSource` is **carried by the car** and the ground pages under a vehicle.

> **1 car resident on both hosts, the same one; the hero enters on both;
> 34.1 m in 300 steps, top 16.81 m/s, 1 018 wheel contacts of a possible 1 200;
> and the two hosts are BYTE-IDENTICAL for all 300 steps** — plus a per-step
> comparison of wheels-grounded and forward speed to the bit, because a
> whole-world byte compare can hide a car inside a big number.

It is a sharper instrument for the streaming claim than the arm it joins: the
source is now a body whose four wheel rays read whatever ground has paged in, so
a tile that arrived on one host and not the other separates the traces within a
step or two. The engine is asserted from the same trace — **1 `Play`, 334
`SetPitch`, 334 `SetVolume`, revs sweeping 0.0000 to 0.4944** — because a count
arm alone passes on a constant cue.

*(The audio clause's first cut read `(0, 300, 300)` and the loop was right: the
one `Play` is emitted on the step the rig is **derived**, long before anybody is
driving it. The instrument was late, not the feature.)*

**THE CONNECTIVITY WALK — open item 16 dies.**
`every_settlement_is_reachable_from_every_other_over_the_built_road_graph` builds
a real `inf_gis::RoadGraph::from_layer` over the committed roads layer — the same
function `inf_island::roads::build_mesh` builds one with, on the same bytes — and
routes every ordered site pair with `inf_nav::route` over the graph's own
`nav_graph()`. **Not** over the route list, which is the *input* to the junction
derivation and cannot falsify it: two roads that cross without sharing an endpoint
are two routes and one junction-free graph, which is exactly the defect a topology
claim has to be able to see.

| island | segments | intersections | junctions | length | ordered pairs | longest route |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Vancouver Island** | 11 | 7 | **7** | 33.74 km | **42, all reachable** | 8.08 km |
| Island Fixture | 1 | 2 | 0 | 1.37 km | 2, all reachable | 1.37 km |

**THE GRADE PROMISE, DRIVEN.** I7's ledger says its audit *"says a car could
climb it"*; nothing in this repository had ever put a car on that slope.
`editor/crates/inf-editor-core/tests/vehicle_grade.rs` reads the worst **planned**
stretch off both committed route layers — **0.0810 against the island's own 0.080
ceiling, 0.0993 against the fixture's 0.100** — and then drives the steeper number
I7's audit found against the *built terrain*, **0.108**:

> the catalogue's **1 185 kg sedan** covers **282.1 m in fifteen seconds**, gains
> **30.51 m**, and tops out at **26.19 m/s (94 km/h)**. Its control is a 0.60
> grade, where the same car goes **−54.0 m** — without it, an arm would pass
> perfectly for a car sliding uphill on a bug.

The truck climbs it too and is a different car: **97.9 m and +10.61 m** against
the sedan's 156.1 and +16.91 over ten seconds, which is what a heavier row geared
to a lower top speed has to look like.

### Clause 5 — the ledger

**What a car costs the island's step.** Release, the cooked fixture island with
the hero driving, mean of ninety driving steps after the ground has paged and the
springs have settled:

| station | ms | | station | ms |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `solver` | 6.8826 | | `crowd` | 0.0720 |
| `animation` | 3.4523 | | `camera` | 0.0441 |
| `physics3d sync` | 2.1954 | | `deformation` | 0.0408 |
| `terrain stream` | 0.2541 | | `propagate` | 0.0346 |
| `write-back` | 0.2110 | | `cell stream` | 0.0159 |
| `character move` | 0.1784 | | `society` | 0.0115 |
| `gameplay` | 0.1699 | | `audio` | 0.0102 |
| | | | **`vehicle`** | **0.0070** |
| **the whole step** | **13.6109 ms** | | | |

**The `vehicle` row is 0.0070 ms for one car against a 0.5 ms ceiling at
sixty-four**, and the phase is asserted to have *run* before it is asserted to
have been cheap: a budget met by a door that returned early is a budget about
nothing.

**The frame is not re-measured, and that is a claim rather than an omission.**
This wave adds no pass, no batch, no draw-call kind and no golden: a sedan is
**eight `MeshInstance`s** — four body parts and four tyres, the wheel entities
themselves drawing nothing — through the path an authored actor has always
taken, and the island's own frame is a settlement of 365 545 scattered
instances. Seven cars is fifty-six instances against that, and the projector
walks them in the loop it already walks. What a car *would* cost a frame is a
question about a fleet, and the fleet is VEH1b's.

### Carried, by name

1. **The engine's emitter does not MOVE.** `AudioCommand` has no `SetPosition`,
   and `AudioEngine::set_position` has existed since P12.3 with **exactly one
   caller, which is a test** — the `set_debris_budget` shape, for the seventh
   time. So a driving car's engine is spatialized where its `Play` was issued and
   fades as the car drives away from its own spawn. The zero-new-API constraint
   was the brief's and it is met; the fix is one enum variant, one drain arm and
   one mirrored line in each host, and it is a decision with its own arms.
2. **The phase-29 course's car is still built sideways** — 4.0 × 1.0 × 2.0 m over
   a 1.8 m track and a 2.8 m wheelbase. Tripwired by
   `the_phase29_courses_car_is_still_wider_than_it_is_long`; the fix is a
   re-proportion plus a re-bless of a committed level with a twenty-arm gate.
3. **No car golden.** The four ADDITIVE pins (the phase18 name array and three
   count/digest pairs) were **not moved** and the set stays at 59. A car has no
   committed frame, and every claim this wave makes is asserted as *state*.
4. **A car exists only in an active cell.** The fixture has two cars and **one**
   is resident at boot, which is the coverage number the drive gate quotes. That
   is the partition working — a car parked at a settlement nobody has visited does
   not exist until they arrive — and it means the shipped island's seven are
   asserted at the level, not in a running sim.
5. **The wheel-ray normal is measured, unread and tripwired.** The smoothing
   question re-opens the day a class reads `WheelContact::normal`, with the
   0.0643° / 15.6898° table already measured.
6. **The ≤ 5 cm cross-section bound is measured on open ground, not on the
   circuit.** The ray-versus-`height_at` gap is 0.039784 m at 0.15 m of DTM
   relief; the levelled road corridor's own chord error is the I2 audit's
   0.000750 m. Nothing re-measured the island's *drawn* cross-section against the
   heightfield at speed, because the road mesh has no collider to cast against.
7. **Traffic is VEH1b's**: no lane centrelines, no path-following controller, no

8. **The catalogue has no runtime loader.** `VehicleDefs::merge_toml` is consumed

10. **The drive gate is 300 steps and the island drive is 900.** Ten seconds of
